invariants.name: density_equals_reduced_coordinates
invariants.invariant: representation equivalence: the ZerosumNormal log-density at a zerosum point x must equal the log-density of N(0, sigma^2 I) evaluated in any orthonormal reduced-coordinate basis of the zerosum subspace, i.e. -D/2*log(2*pi*sigma^2) - ||s||^2/(2*sigma^2) with D = prod(n_i - 1)
invariants.rationale: this is exactly the 'independently validated reduced-coordinate implementation' referenced in the problem statement. Pre-fix the logp is the elementwise normal logp scaled by D/N, which keeps the correct constant but wrong quadratic coefficient, so it disagrees with the reduced-coordinate density by (1 - D/N)*||s||^2/(2*sigma^2) (~1.2 for the (3,4) test point); post-fix they agree to ~1e-15. Uses a new (3,4) support and sigma=0.9, unrelated to the public fixture.

invariants.name: density_normalizes_to_unit_mass
invariants.invariant: conservation of probability mass: the ZerosumNormal density integrated over the whole zerosum subspace must equal 1 (it is a probability density, not just a kernel)
invariants.rationale: numerical tensor-product quadrature over the orthonormal subspace coordinates gives total mass 2.000 on a (2,2) support pre-fix (analytically exactly 2 for the scaled kernel) and ~1.000 post-fix (quadrature error < 0.005). A wrong density constant/curvature cannot in general preserve unit mass. Probes two new supports (2,2) and (3,3) with new sigma values 1.7 and 0.8.

invariants.name: scale_parameter_consistency
invariants.invariant: scale/unit consistency of a Gaussian density: logp(x; c*sigma) - logp(x; sigma) must equal -D*log(c) + (1 - 1/c^2)*||x||^2/(2*sigma^2) for any rescale factor c, independent of support size
invariants.rationale: this is a metamorphic relation between two runs at different scales rather than an absolute formula. Pre-fix the quadratic term carries the wrong factor D/N (for the (3,4) grid, 6/12), so the observed sigma->2*sigma shift is -3.321 instead of the required -2.483 on three new random points; post-fix the identity holds to 1e-8. New support (3,4), sigma=0.9, c=2.0.

invariants.name: joint_density_matches_reduced_coordinates
invariants.invariant: representation equivalence at the model level: the joint density (grand-mean prior + centered lab/protocol/interaction ZerosumNormal priors + cell likelihood) of the factorial calibration model must equal the joint density of the identical model reparameterized in orthonormal reduced coordinates; this is the condition under which the posteriors (and hence the planned contrasts and their uncertainties) agree
invariants.rationale: directly encodes the problem statement: the buggy logp made the posterior of the centered model differ from the reduced-coordinate implementation. On a new 3-lab x 4-protocol study with new scales (tau=0.8, noise=0.4) and synthetic data, the pre-fix joint density differs from the reduced-coordinate joint by (1-D/N)*||effect||^2/(2*tau^2) per effect term (~2.5 at the first random point); post-fix the two joint densities agree to <1e-6 at three points, so the posteriors are identical in exact arithmetic. No MCMC is used, keeping the comparison exact and reproducible.

invariants.name: moments_match_projected_normal
invariants.invariant: boundary/moment behavior: the ZerosumNormal with scalar sigma is the unconstrained normal N(0, sigma^2 I) restricted to the zerosum subspace (per the docstring, ZSN(sigma) = N(0, sigma^2 (I - J/n))), so its second moments in orthonormal subspace coordinates must be sigma^2 * I
invariants.rationale: checks the density's curvature (precision), which is where the bug lives, via a different observable than the absolute logp. Numerical moment extraction from the density on a new 1-axis support of size 5 (D=4) with sigma=1.3 gives covariance sigma^2*N/D = 2.1125 per coordinate pre-fix (max deviation 0.4225 from sigma^2=1.69) versus sigma^2*I to quadrature accuracy post-fix. A fix that only tuned the additive constant (e.g. the public smoke behavior) would still fail this.

notes: All five tests were executed on the pre-fix tree (repo reverted to baseline multivariate.py) and on the patched tree: all 5 FAIL with AssertionError pre-fix (magnitudes: logp offset ~1.2, total mass 2.0 vs 1, scale-shift error ~0.84, joint-density gap ~2.5, covariance deviation 0.4225) and all 5 PASS post-fix (tolerances 1e-8/0.01). Shapes (3,4), (2,2), (3,3), (5,), 3x4 study and all scales/realizations are new; the public 4x5 fixture, its scales (2.0/0.7/0.6/0.5) and its seed are not used anywhere. I did not add an MCMC posterior-sampling test: invariant 4's exact joint-density equivalence is the deterministic version of the same property the problem statement describes (posterior must match the reduced-coordinate implementation), and it avoids NUTS noise. Batched (batch-dim) logp additivity was investigated but is NOT a discriminator: the pre-fix code applies the same per-draw D/N scaling to batched and unbatched values, so additivity holds pre-fix as well.
